conflict: Two lanes run today reached OPPOSITE conclusions about dropping lm_head from Q8 to Q4 on mixed-1p5.

lane_a.name: qwen38-attention-density
lane_a.basis: 34 CPU probes on real BF16 weights and real captured activations; cosine-based quality screen
lane_a.own_caveat: states 'lm_head q3 only after a greedy generate-and-compare on both models. Cosine is not enough.'

lane_b.name: q80-terminal-head
lane_b.action: leave lm_head and embed at HGRAVU01 bits=8; Q4 overlay FORBIDDEN
lane_b.basis: CPU quality screen n=384 measuring GREEDY FLIPS vs source BF16
lane_b.measurement: Q4 lm_head produces 11-13 greedy flips; Q3 37; Q2/binary ~100; SVD r256 349

RESOLUTION: Lane B wins ON LM_HEAD. It measured emitted-token behaviour directly; lane A screened on cosine and says itself that cosine is not enough for this tensor. A logit error becomes the emitted token with no downstream layer to absorb it, so behavioural evidence outranks a distance metric here.
NOT_IN_CONFLICT: Attention. Lane B scoped itself to lm_head and embed and did not evaluate attention. Lane A's attention finding stands: mixed-1p5 OVER-PROTECTS attention at Q8, and dropping attention alone to Q4 is a large cheap byte win.

agreed_action.attention: Q8 -> Q4 on mixed-1p5. Supported by lane A, not contradicted by lane B.
agreed_action.lm_head: STAYS Q8. Lane B's 11-13 greedy flips at Q4 is decisive.

why_this_matters_for_G003: Q80 mixed moves 2.218 GB/token. The rung instrument put rung C (200 TPS) at <=2.06 GB, so it was the one rung blocked by bytes. Dropping attention to Q4 moves that budget - but the exact saving must be recomputed with lm_head HELD at Q8, since the -925 MB figure bundles both tensors.
method_note: This is the disagreement-protocol case: two lanes disagreeing is more informative than either alone, and the resolution is by evidence QUALITY - behavioural greedy-id measurement over a cosine proxy - not by averaging or by recency.
